doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: Tribute album to Buddy Johnson
summary: Houston Person suggested the tribute; Norman Simmons plays on it, and Houston chose the musicians.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Tell me about this recent recording. After all these years what prompted the tribute to Buddy?

Well actually we kept saying it. Houston was always saying well why don’t you do — I said yeah because he was my first boss. And we’d let it slide and let it slide, and then Houston brought it up again, because it was his idea. “Why don’t you do a tribute to Buddy Johnson and do all of his songs.” And I said yeah that would be nice. Because I liked all of his songs, because I think he wrote beautiful tunes. And I was so grateful to him too because he was the beginning of my career.
And Norman Simmons plays on it?

Norman Simmons, yeah. Houston got the group together, because he always knows. If I’m going to record certain songs he wants certain musicians he thinks would be best for that type of music I’m doing. So I listen to him. It hasn’t been bad so far.
